explainBack.question: Why doesn't installing the Gemini Windows app mean Gemini can now read your screen, files or email automatically?
explainBack.answer: Because the app only changes the entry route into the same online service. Alt + Space opens a window beside your work, but Gemini receives only what you actively give it: text you paste, an image you upload, or Google apps like Gmail and Drive that you explicitly choose to connect. Account controls also persist—on a managed work account, the administrator must have enabled Gemini at all. The door is new; the shop's rules about what comes inside are unchanged.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: P004 (same shop, different door), P006 (upload and connection are choices you make), P009 (explicitly denies automatic screen/file access), P010 (account controls and limits survive the desktop app).
explainBack.assessment: The artifact fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; the opt-in nature of sharing and the persistence of admin controls are both explicit, so an attentive reader can reconstruct the reasoning unaided.

unseenTransfer.scenario: A reader's colleague installs the Gemini app on her company-managed laptop, signs in with her work account, and the app refuses to work. Meanwhile she assumes that once it does work, it will automatically summarise the confidential contract PDF open on her screen.
unseenTransfer.question: Using only this article's mechanism, what explains the refusal, and is her assumption about the open PDF correct?
unseenTransfer.answer: The refusal is explained by P005: a work or school account needs Gemini enabled by its administrator, and on a managed account that administrator controls availability—so her IT admin likely hasn't turned it on; the fix is asking IT, not reinstalling. Her assumption is wrong per P006 and P009: the app has no automatic view of her screen or open files. It would only see the contract if she deliberately pasted or uploaded it—which, for a confidential document, P006's rule (only share material you are comfortable using with the service) says she should first weigh against company policy.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: P005 for the admin gate on managed accounts; P006 and P009 for opt-in sharing and no automatic screen access; P008 for checking which account and what to share before use.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The transfer succeeds: both the eligibility failure and the false automatic-access assumption resolve directly from the article's route-vs-function and opt-in-connection mechanism, with no facts needed beyond the artifact.
